title: Together, twenty-seven times
hook: prayer in congregation is twenty-seven times better than alone (Bukhari)

segments.voice: Yesterday, istikharah: two units and a du'a that asks God to choose the good. Today the prayer stops being alone.

Sunset in a small apartment, two roommates home from work, a pot on the stove. The sunset prayer has come in. Each could pray alone, in separate rooms, and be back at dinner in minutes. Instead one steps forward onto the rug, and the other stands at his right side. One voice says Allahu akbar, and two people bow at once. No mosque, no crowd, no microphone. A leader, a follower, and a room that smells of onions. Today's word is what those two just made.
screen: `SUNSET, TWO ROOMMATES.` → `ONE STEPS FORWARD.` → `ONE VOICE, TWO BOW.`

segments.voice: Jama'ah means congregation, the gathered group. First, the number in today's title. Ibn Umar reported, in Sahih al-Bukhari, that the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ said prayer in congregation is better than prayer alone by twenty-seven degrees. Right beside it, Bukhari records another companion's report that says twenty-five. Scholars offer ways to read the two together; the hadith doesn't explain the arithmetic. Both agree on direction: together is more. Second, the Qur'an. Pickthall's translation of surah two: "bow your heads with those who bow." With. Third, the rows. The Prophet told them to straighten their rows, and said straightening them is part of establishing the prayer. Anas, his servant, described them standing shoulder to shoulder and foot to foot. In a row, the person beside you is whoever arrived next, and the row doesn't check anyone's bank balance. Fourth, who is called. Scholars differ on how binding congregation is for men: the Hanbali school treats it as obligatory, others as a communal duty or a strongly stressed sunnah. And Bukhari records the Prophet saying: do not keep the women servants of God from the mosques of God. Now look back at the week. Stand now, at the iqamah. The sunnah around it. End the night odd. Awake for him. The forenoon prayer. Choose for me. All but the first can be done alone, in a dark bedroom or a quiet office. The week ends by stepping into the row.
screen: `TWENTY-SEVEN, OR TWENTY-FIVE.` · `BOW WITH THOSE WHO BOW.` · `SHOULDER TO SHOULDER.` · `THE WEEK STEPS INTO THE ROW.` · then, large: `TOGETHER IS MORE.`

segments.voice: See a row in your mind and who might stand in it with you, a neighbor, a parent, a stranger from the bus, and feel where your shoulder would touch theirs. If you pray, you can pray one prayer today in congregation, at a mosque or with even one other person at home. If you don't, you can share one thing you'd usually do alone: a meal, a walk, a job around the house.
Jama'ah. The congregation: prayer in rows, together, counted in the hadith as twenty-seven degrees above prayer alone. Today's word.
Your line: together is more. Tomorrow, the voice that speaks to the row on Friday.

howItsDone: Muslims pray in congregation at mosques, in homes and at work, standing in straight rows behind an imam; even two people can pray together, with one leading.

chat.says: Why pray together at home? Isn't praying alone in your room just as good?
options: A hadith says praying together beats praying alone by twenty-seven degrees, even with two.
It's the same reward either way; praying together only matters on a Friday.
It only counts as a congregation inside a mosque, with a crowd and a proper imam.
chat.meaning: Ibn Umar's report gives twenty-seven degrees, another gives twenty-five; both agree together is more. Two roommates on a rug make a congregation.

jama'ah.meaning: the congregation, praying together in rows

sunnah.meaning: the Prophet's practice; here, a stressed voluntary act

notes: Editor: new hook (two roommates praying together at home) because the old one, a room forming rows at the iqamah, repeated day 1079's hook almost scene for scene; the teach line that pointed back to it was rewritten. The week look-back now quotes day 1080's carry exactly ('the sunnah around it'). Non-Hanbali view widened to 'a communal duty or a strongly stressed sunnah' in voice and myth.
Week end (days 1079–1085): the teach looks back at the week's carries using the index lines for 1079–1084 (1079–1081 were not on disk when this was written).
Bukhari 645 (Ibn Umar, 27) and 646 (Abu Sa'id, 25): confirm numbering and companions.

Pickthall 2:43 quoted from memory as part of 'Establish worship, pay the poor-due, and bow your heads with those who bow (in worship)'; the parenthesis is omitted by ending the quotation before it. Confirm.
Bukhari 723 (straightening rows), 725 (Anas: shoulder to shoulder, foot to foot), 900 (do not prevent the women servants of Allah from the mosques of Allah): confirm numbers.

Fiqh summary: Hanbali school holds congregation obligatory (fard 'ayn) for men; others (Hanafi, Maliki, many Shafi'is) a stressed sunnah or communal duty. Simplified to 'others ... a strongly stressed sunnah'; Keeper may want 'communal obligation' added for the Shafi'i view.
The iqamah of 1079 is a congregational call, hence 'all but the first can be done alone'.
